lessons.title: DOM → CSSOM → Render Tree → Layout → Paint → Composite Pipeline
lessons.description: The browser converts your HTML and CSS into pixels through a multi-step rendering pipeline.

sections.heading: The rendering pipeline
paragraphs: When the browser renders a page, it goes through several steps: parsing HTML into the DOM, CSS into the CSSOM, combining them into a render tree, calculating layout, painting pixels, and compositing layers.
list: DOM — HTML is parsed into a tree of nodes
CSSOM — CSS rules are parsed into a tree of styles
Render Tree — DOM + CSSOM combined (visible elements only)
Layout — calculate exact position and size of each element
Paint — fill in pixels (text, colors, images, borders)
Composite — combine layers into the final visible page

codeExamples.heading: Pipeline trigger example
explanation: Changing geometric properties (width, height, position) triggers layout.
Changing visual properties (color, visibility) only triggers repaint.
Reading layout properties forces a synchronous layout calculation.
Batch reads before writes to avoid layout thrashing.

practice.task: Write code that triggers layout thrashing by alternating reads and writes to element dimensions. Then refactor to batch reads and writes.
hints: Thrashing: for (let el of elements) { el.offsetWidth; el.style.width = "100px"; }.
Batched: read all widths first, then write all styles.

keyTakeaways: The rendering pipeline: DOM → CSSOM → Render Tree → Layout → Paint → Composite.
Geometric changes trigger layout; visual changes only trigger repaint.
Layout thrashing (alternating reads and writes) kills performance.
Always batch layout reads before writes.
lessons.challenge: Use Chrome DevTools Performance panel to visualize the rendering pipeline for a page with many DOM updates.

lessons.title: Understanding Reflow vs Repaint Triggers
lessons.description: Reflow recalculates layout; repaint redraws pixels. Minimize both for smooth performance.

sections.heading: Reflow vs Repaint
list: Reflow always triggers repaint; repaint never triggers reflow
Minimize reflows by batching DOM changes

sections.heading: What triggers reflow?
list: Changing width, height, margin, padding, border

codeExamples.heading: Minimizing reflows
explanation: Each innerHTML change triggers a reflow — 100 changes = 100 reflows.
DocumentFragment collects all changes in memory, then adds them at once.
Other techniques: CSS transforms, will-change, and requestAnimationFrame.

practice.task: Create 1000 DOM elements using innerHTML in a loop (slow) vs DocumentFragment (fast). Measure the time difference.

keyTakeaways: Reflow recalculates layout (expensive); repaint redraws pixels (cheaper).
Reflow always triggers repaint; batch DOM changes to minimize reflows.
DocumentFragment collects changes and applies them in one reflow.
Avoid reading layout properties inside loops — read once, use the value.
lessons.challenge: Profile a list rendering operation in DevTools and identify reflow events.

lessons.title: Avoiding Layout Thrashing & Scheduling with requestAnimationFrame
lessons.description: Use requestAnimationFrame to sync DOM updates with the browser's frame cycle for smooth 60fps rendering.

sections.heading: requestAnimationFrame
list: Syncs your code with the browser's refresh cycle (typically 60fps)
Automatically paused when the tab is not visible
Preferred for animations and visual updates

codeExamples.heading: Smooth animation with rAF
explanation: requestAnimationFrame runs before the browser paints — no wasted frames.
It's automatically throttled when the tab is hidden.
Batch visual updates inside rAF for smooth 60fps rendering.
Never use setTimeout for animations — it's not synced with the paint cycle.

practice.task: Create a smooth scrolling animation using requestAnimationFrame that moves an element across the screen over 2 seconds.
hints: Apply easing for a natural feel.

keyTakeaways: requestAnimationFrame syncs your code with the browser's paint cycle.
Always use rAF for animations — never setTimeout or setInterval.
rAF is automatically paused when the tab is hidden.
Batch DOM updates inside rAF for smooth 60fps rendering.
lessons.challenge: Build a parallax scrolling effect using requestAnimationFrame that responds to scroll position.
